name: Combinatorial Eluder Dimension
definition: For a binary class $\mathcal H$ and base hypothesis $h^*\in\mathcal H$, $\mathrm{Edim}_{h^*}(\mathcal H)$ is the largest $m$ for which there are points $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and hypotheses $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in\mathcal H$ such that $h_i(x_i)\ne h^*(x_i)$ while $h_i(x_j)=h^*(x_j)$ for every $j<i$. The **combinatorial eluder dimension** is $\max_{h^*\in\mathcal H}\mathrm{Edim}_{h^*}(\mathcal H)$.
graph_summary: Longest sequential disagreement witness relative to one base hypothesis; the binary specialization of eluder dimension.
description: This is the binary combinatorial specialization, rather than the scale-sensitive real-valued eluder dimension of Russo and Van Roy.
origin_references: Eluder dimension was introduced by Russo and Van Roy in \cite{russo2013eluder}; this binary formulation and its comparisons are developed in \cite{li2022understanding}.

monotonic.proof: A sequential witness in a subfamily is still a witness after the class is enlarged.

p_monotonic.proof: A witness in a coordinate projection lifts by choosing preimages of its base and witness hypotheses; all required equalities and disagreements are on retained coordinates.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, so it follows from the two preceding monotonicities.

doubly_monotonic.proof: It is monotonic both under subfamilies and under coordinate projections.
